meta.title: About GnomeVPN
meta.description: Why GnomeVPN runs on Hysteria2, how the infrastructure is built, what we do not log, and why the tunnel is delivered through INCY.

title: About the service
intro: Short and without the marketing: how this works inside and why we made these choices.

problem.title: The problem we set out to solve
problem.body: Classic TCP-based VPN protocols are unstable on many networks: the connection drops a few minutes after data starts flowing, and changing port or server helps only briefly. We wanted a connection that holds all day — on mobile data, on the road, in a hotel.

protocol.title: Why Hysteria2
protocol.body: Hysteria2 runs over QUIC — the transport of HTTP/3 — over UDP. QUIC copes better with packet loss, so on mobile data and weak Wi-Fi the connection is steadier and speed drops less.

noLogs.title: What we do not store
noLogs.body: We keep no record of your connections: which sites you opened, or when. For each device all that remains is the time it was last active — a single value that is overwritten — and the amount of data moved, for the counter in the app. The full list of what we store is in the privacy policy.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.body: Nodes are rented from several providers in different countries, each set up automatically from the same script. When a node stops answering it drops out of the list in the app on its own, with nothing for you to do.

client.title: About the app
client.body: The client is INCY — a free third-party app that we do not develop. That is the honest arrangement: rather than spend years chasing someone else's feature set on five platforms, we hand you a standard subscription link. It works in other compatible clients too — you are not locked in.

honesty.title: What we do not promise
honesty.body: We do not promise it will work everywhere forever: networks change, and sometimes nodes have to change with them. We do not promise anonymity — a VPN hides traffic from your ISP, it does not make you invisible. If the service is not for you, we refund the unused period — write to us within 14 days of paying.
